answer: Each identity is bound to one enclave chip, whose crystal measurement of its code is signed by a counter that cannot roll back. The registry takes one identity per counter value, so an oasis of virtual copies mints nothing: the second registration is rejected. The inlet admits one chip at a time, and the kth fake identity needs a kth chip at about $80, so 1,000 fakes cost $80,000 in hardware that cannot be reused. Chip rental fails because the rented counter advances publicly and cannot be rented twice, while one honest chip keeps its full share.
